subject: maths
title: Finding the equation of a line

scenes.heading: Finding the equation of a line
scenes.sub: Two facts are all you need
scenes.say: If you know a point and a slope, or just two points, you can write the equation of a line. Then you can predict any value on it.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Stand in one spot and aim a laser at a fixed angle
scenes.science: A point and a gradient fix exactly one line
scenes.breaks: A laser beam goes one way from the pointer; a line extends forever in both directions.
scenes.say: Picture standing in one spot and aiming a laser pointer at a fixed angle. The beam's path is completely decided. A point is where you stand, and the gradient is your aim. One difference: a line goes both ways forever.

scenes.heading: The point–gradient formula
parts: a known point on the line
scenes.say: The point gradient formula is y minus y one equals m times, x minus x one. Substitute the gradient and a point, then expand and make y the subject.
scenes.caption: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁): substitute m and a point, then expand and make y the subject.

scenes.heading: From two points
scenes.question: Find the line through (−1, 4) and (3, −4).
scenes.say: Find the line through negative one, four and three, negative four. Gradient first: negative eight over four is negative two. Then y minus four equals negative two times, x plus one. Expand and add four: y equals negative two x plus two.
scenes.caption: m = −8 ÷ 4 = −2. y − 4 = −2(x + 1), so y = −2x + 2.

scenes.heading: Reading a line from a graph
scenes.say: From a graph: first the axes, then the line. It crosses the y-axis at three, so c is three. From negative two, zero to zero, three, it rises three and runs two, so the gradient is one point five. The line is y equals one point five x plus three.
scenes.caption: c = 3. Rise 3, run 2, so m = 1.5. y = 1.5x + 3.

scenes.heading: Perpendicular: flip and switch
scenes.say: Perpendicular lines meet at right angles, and their gradients multiply to negative one. Here is y equals two thirds x plus one. Flip two thirds and switch the sign: negative three halves. Through four, negative one, that gives y equals negative one point five x plus five.
scenes.caption: Perpendicular gradients multiply to −1. ⅔ → −3/2. Through (4, −1): y = −1.5x + 5.

points: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁), then tidy up
scenes.say: Recap. You need a gradient and a point, or two points. Use the point gradient formula, then make y the subject. Parallel lines share a gradient, and perpendicular gradients multiply to negative one. Now try the practice questions!
